summary: Follow-up on Dec 17 outage where Aurora's production service saw elevated latencies and partial degradation. Discussed root cause (autoscaler/quantization rollout interaction + KV cache growth), short-term mitigations, runbook updates, and next steps toward Dedicated capacity and reliability improvements.
transcript:
[00:00] Ben Carter: hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll keep this tight, 45 minutes. we ran through the draft postmortem earlier, this is the follow-up to align actions.
[00:22] Liam O'Neill: thanks Ben, appreciate quick turnaround on the deck. team is still a bit shook from yesterday, major customer calls.
[00:35] Maya Singh: quick recap for folks - incident started 11:42 UTC, backend GPU nodes started to spike memory then autoscaler tripped, we saw cascading cold starts which increased tail latency. there was a quantization experiment on the new model variant that increased KV cache pressure and caused unexpected OOMs.
[01:05] Priya Patel: just to be clear, we had a canary at 5% but the rollout policy allowed simultaneous parallel replicas, so when a node OOMed it redistributed requests and the autoscaler reacted to CPU not memory so it didn't recover quick enough.
[01:35] Dana Ruiz: one security note - audit logs show multiple failed auth calls during failover, likely benign but we want to keep them for compliance.
[01:50] Ben Carter: thanks. root cause in short: (a) model variant with slightly different memory characteristics + quantization changes, (b) autoscaler config prioritized CPU, not memory, (c) no circuit breaker to stop rollout when error rate jumped.
[02:12] Liam O'Neill: question - why didn't prefix/KV caching prevent this? I thought cache would reduce new token compute.
[02:25] Maya Singh: it usually does but the quantized variant uses a different KV layout; there's a bug in the runtime path where KV growth isn't bounded for that variant - effectively K-V cash grew until OOM. apologies, that's on us to fix.
[02:50] Priya Patel: we also saw a bunch of S3 timeouts during spikes that made controller api slower, so that compounded recovery time.
[03:12] Ben Carter: ok, mitigation timeline we proposed: immediate (hotfix) - rollback quantized variant to v2026-12-10 baseline for a temporary window, enable a memory-focused autoscaler metric, add circuit-breaker to stop canary if 5xx>2% for 3 minutes. mid-term - runtime patch to bound KV growth, add memory overcommit detection, extended smoke tests. long-term - Dedicated capacity option and better observability.
[03:48] Liam O'Neill: timeline wise we need the rollback and autoscaler change today, can you commit to that?
[03:55] Maya Singh: yes, we can schedule rollback in the next maintenance window, target 18:00 UTC today; autoscaler toggle is config only, we'll push the memory metric rule in 2 hours.
[04:10] Dana Ruiz: for compliance we need full request/response logs for the incident window, redacted PII. can you provide the logs to our secure bucket?
[04:22] Ben Carter: yes, we'll get the redacted logs uploaded by EOD tomorrow.
[04:30] Priya Patel: also want explicit SLA impact calculation for finance. were any requests dropped vs just slowed?
[04:38] Maya Singh: we observed increased 503s for ~7 minutes during peak; rough ballpark is 0.8% error rate on that hour, we'll run precise analysis.
[04:55] Liam O'Neill: we are evaluating Dedicated capacity because this unpredictability is a blocker. can you outline steps for a pilot and expected lead times?
[05:10] Ben Carter: yes - pilot process: scope GPU count/region, provisioning (1-2 weeks depending on availability), we can do a month-long reserved pool with canaries, Redwood will provide runbook + support for migration. Maya, can you put a pilot proposal together?
[05:25] Maya Singh: will do; include cost estimates and fallback plan to hosted.
[05:33] Ben Carter: competitor note - you mentioned Anthropic earlier, sound like you're still data-checking multi-vendor options?
[05:40] Liam O'Neill: yes, we are running evaluations but our primary concern is predictable performance & auditability.
[05:50] Maya Singh: action items recap: we'll share the final postmortem doc, logs, and a canary rollback schedule. on the eng side we'll open a bug for runtime KV bound, and a config change for autoscaler.
[06:10] Priya Patel: please include a detailed runbook change that covers detection -> mitigation -> restore steps; our oncall needs clear instructions.
[06:22] Ben Carter: agreed, we'll draft runbook and a short playbook for your oncall.
[06:30] Dana Ruiz: double-check SSO audit artifacts - Sam-L assertions and KMS logs, we need those for SOC2 evidence.
[06:42] Maya Singh: we'll pull KMS access logs and SSO traces, note that some names might be redacted in transit.
[06:55] Liam O'Neill: ok last Q - any stop-gap in the runtime to prevent unbounded KV growth until the fix ships?
[07:05] Maya Singh: yes we can introduce a soft-limit in the runtime to evict old prefix entries after X MB and fail fast on heavy growth; it's a low-risk change and we can gate it behind a feature flag. aim 3-5 days to test and roll.
[07:25] Ben Carter: great, let's capture due dates. I'm going to send an updated timeline and schedule the rollback.
[07:35] Priya Patel: thanks everyone, appreciate the speed.
[07:40] Ben Carter: meeting wrap - recap of next steps and we'll meet again next week if needed.
[07:46] END TRANSCRIPT
